title: Whole-Roos normalization of point-system transport and sections
statement:
Fix $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Set $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, let $h=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ for geometric Frobenius [def-trf-scheme-frobenius], and on the small pro-etale site set $B_n=(A_n)_s$ and $\widehat R_s=\lim_nB_n$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $\mathscr S_s$ be the abelian category of strict $B_n$-module systems with quotient-linear transitions, with its ordinary unbounded derived category [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Write $U_s$ for levelwise restriction to $\widehat R_s$-module towers and $\mathcal L_s=R\lim U_s$ [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Put $F_r=(h^r)^{-1}$ on module complexes with scalars transported through the canonical coefficient isomorphisms, and $G_r$ for its levelwise functor on systems [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image, def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. Read the finite levels through $j_{r,M}:F_rM\to(h^r)^*M$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, of part (a) of the latter definition. Let $\Gamma_\bullet$ be restriction of scalars followed by exact sections levelwise, retaining all transitions [def-trf-coefficient-tower-operations, lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact].

Use the natural maps $u_{r,M}$ and their localizations $I_{r,C}$ specified by [lem-trf-point-system-transport-descent]. For a strict tower complex $X$ of $\widehat R_s$-modules, or of $R$-modules, write
$$H(X)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_X)[-1],\quad H(X)^i=(\prod_nX_n^{i-1})\oplus(\prod_nX_n^i),\quad d(b,a)=(-db-(1-s_X)a,da),$$
where $s_X((x_n)_n)=(t_nx_{n+1})_n$ for the actual transitions $t_n$. Use the natural normalized identification of this functor with TOTAL derived limit [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]; its strict augmentation has zero shifted coordinate. Countable products of sheaf modules are sectionwise and exact [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact], as are products of $R$-modules.

For every $C\in D(\mathscr S_s)$, with no completeness or constructibility restriction on $N=\mathcal L_sC$, the canonical product comparisons for $F_r$ and $\Gamma(s,-)$ give natural isomorphisms
$$a_{r,C}:F_r\mathcal L_sC\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L_sG_rC,\qquad \zeta_C:R\lim\Gamma_\bullet C\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(s,\mathcal L_sC).$$
Their normalization is that of [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit]: on a strict representative $M$, $a$ is the canonical $F_r(\prod X_n)\cong\prod F_rX_n$ comparison on BOTH coordinates of $H(U_sM)$ (including the level identifications $j_r$), and $\zeta$ is the inverse of the analogous exact-sections comparison. There is no off-diagonal component. Equivalently these are the comparisons obtained by applying inverse image or sections to the entire limit cone on tower resolutions.

Let $\sigma_{r,K}:\Gamma(s,K)\to\Gamma(s,F_rK)$ denote the restriction/colimit-insertion/sheafification recipe of [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport] on any completed-module complex $K$, localized by exactness. Then, as an equality of derived maps on WHOLE towers,
$$\zeta_{G_rC}\circ R\lim(I_{r,C})=\Gamma(s,a_{r,C})\circ\sigma_{r,\mathcal L_sC}\circ\zeta_C.$$
More explicitly, on a strict representative, $R\lim(I_{r,C})$ in these normalized coordinates is the actual diagonal chain map
$$H(u_r)(b,a)=((\prod_nu_{r,n})b,(\prod_nu_{r,n})a),\qquad (1-s_{\Gamma_\bullet G_rM})\prod_nu_{r,n}=(\prod_nu_{r,n})(1-s_{\Gamma_\bullet M}).$$
Here $u_{r,n}$ is the $n$th map after sections, so $H(u_r)$ is between the $R$-module tower cones. After the canonical product comparisons, restriction on each product is $(x_n)_n\mapsto(x_n|_{h^r})_n$ on both coordinates. All the comparisons and the displayed equality are natural for morphisms in $D(\mathscr S_s)$.
